the decline of class was not a result of the rise of Thatcherism but was the product of a long term process of social and political change.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the way in which the Thatcherite project was able to transform this highly conflictual, class based political culture.
how Margaret Thatcher's leadership of the Conservative Party and her subsequent premiership transformed the political culture of the 1970's and 1980's.
the ways in which Thatcherism, as a political project, sought to'make Thatcher's Britain' by 'ditching the class baggge'.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the class struggle was back on the agenda.
the 1960's were a period of social class and social mobility.
the 1970's was a period in which class politics and language were more prominent in the British public sphere than in the previous decade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the class war is over, but the working class won.
the British people have decided that they are no longer governed by their betters.
Thatcher's Britain was not a classless society.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Thatcherite project, far from being an attempt to 'ditch class politics' was actually a continuation of the class politics of the 1970's, but one that took a different tack.
the class politics that dominated the mid 1979s were a thing of the past by the time Thatcher came to power.

Margaret Thatcher's political success was in large part predicated upon her ability to displace the class politics of her opponents and reconfigure the political discourse in ways that were less divisive and more inclusive.
